answer: Forging 105 aliases thus costs 229 bonds held for 17 days each, plus the voyage attestations those aliases can never earn. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an copycat cannot recover it by rotating identities. Each identity must lock a bond, called a thread, before it can post or attest. A single grove checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
